reports.title: The AI cash-flow divide
reports.subtitle: Microsoft's cloud momentum and cash generation contrast with Alphabet's costly expansion.
reports.takeaway: AI revenue expansion remains strong, but the market is discriminating between self-funded growth and widening cash deficits.

items.headline: Azure rose 48%; free cash flow reached $18.6bn.
items.detail: Reuters reported free cash flow of $18.6bn and Azure growth of 48% for the September quarter. Next-quarter Azure growth guidance was 49%–50%. Figures describe that reporting period, not current market prices.

items.headline: Google Cloud doubled, but free cash flow turned negative.
items.detail: Reuters reported September-quarter revenue of $127.6bn and negative free cash flow of $9.07bn. Google Cloud revenue more than doubled.

items.headline: AWS growth expected at 38.2%, according to Reuters' pre-earnings preview.
items.detail: Revenue growth expected at 12.3%. Watch AWS growth, capital spending, financing requirements and free cash flow. These are forecasts, not reported results.

sections.label: Market pulse
sections.text: Cloud and AI demand remain firm. Investors are responding more sharply to cash conversion and capital expenditure than to headline revenue growth.

sections.label: Fixed-income lens
sections.text: A sustained rise in debt-funded AI capex would increase refinancing sensitivity. This is an analytical risk scenario, not a verified bond-market price reaction.

sections.label: Portfolio discipline
sections.text: Compare cash flow after capex, pricing power, guidance and balance-sheet headroom rather than relying only on earnings beats.
